messages.subject: ggtree + unsupervised hierarchical clustering and metadata bar for gHeatmap
messages.subject_clean: ggtree + unsupervised hierarchical clustering and metadata bar for gHeatmap
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am wondering if it is possible to produce a dendrogram over a heatmap plotted with gheatmap(). This would be a useful function, if it is not possible at the moment.

I would like to do two things that I haven't figured out:

1. Perform unsupervised hierarchical clustering on the columns of the heatmap, and have the dendrogram displayed on top of the heatmap, and

2. Add a bar below the columns of the heatmap with numerical metadata about the column (see the last row of the R code below).

Below is a reproducible example that generates a phylogenetic tree and a heatmap from the GlobalPatterns dataset (see attached).

################
rm (list = ls())
library(phyloseq);library(ggstance);library(ggthemes);library(plyr)
library(dplyr);library(ggtree);library(tibble)

# Load sample Phyloseq dataset
data("GlobalPatterns")
GP <- GlobalPatterns
GP <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(GP) > 5000, GP) #just to make the number of OTUs smaller

mergedGP <- merge_samples(GP, "SampleType")
mergedGP <- rarefy_even_depth(mergedGP,rngseed=394582)

print(mergedGP) #final phyloseq object

#make a tree
tr <- phy_tree(mergedGP)
spec <- tax_table(mergedGP) %>% data.frame(stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("otu")
gt <- ggtree(tr, branch.length = "y") %<+% spec
gd <- gt$data

melt_data<-psmelt(mergedGP)

randomHeatmap <- data.frame(replicate(20,sample(0:10000,630,rep=TRUE)))
rownames(randomHeatmap) <- spec$otu

################
# Make a simple dataframe to build the boxplots
melt_simple <- subset(melt_data,select=c(OTU,Sample,Abundance,Kingdom,Phylum))
melt_simple$randomGroup <- sample(2, size = nrow(melt_simple), replace = TRUE)
melt_simple$randomGroup <- as.factor(melt_simple$randomGroup)

t <- get.tax(mergedGP) %>% mutate(PhySpec=paste(Phylum,otu))
taxa_names(mergedGP) <- t$PhySpec
rownames(melt_simple) <-  melt_simple$PhySpec
melt_simple <- as.matrix(melt_simple)

g1 <- gt + geom_tippoint(data=gd$istip,aes(color=Phylum),size=2)
gheatmap(g1,randomHeatmap,offset=1, width=2,colnames_angle=-45,hjust=0,font.size = 2)

metadata <- data.frame(paste("X",1:20,sep=""),"metadata" = rnorm(1:20),row.names = T)

messages.subject_clean: geom_range not correctly displaying 95% HPDs for height from BEAST tree
messages.body_plain:
You use something like this:
ggtree(t) + theme_tree2() +
    geom_range(range='height_0.95_HPD', color='red', alpha=.6, size=2)

and the issue that the ranges are not display on the right places is expected, as length variable is used as branch length, while the range you are using here is height.

Please try the following commands:
ggtree(t, branch.length="height") + theme_tree2() +
    geom_range(range='height_0.95_HPD', color='red', alpha=.6, size=2)

ggtree(t, branch.length="length") + theme_tree2() +
    geom_range(range='length_0.95_HPD', color='red', alpha=.6, size=2)

Hello!

I have two related questions around generating a tree figure using ggtree.

1) I'm working with a large phylogeny in ggtree, and have collapsed and renamed over 100 clades to allow focus on the clades I am interested in.

My basic code is:

p1 = ggtree(tree, layout = 'circular') + geom_tiplab2(color="black")
p2 = collapse(p1, 5406) + geom_cladelabel(node=5406, "Archaea")
p3 = collapse(p2, 5161) + geom_cladelabel(node=5161, "Chloroflexi")
p4 = collapse(p3, 5154) + geom_cladelabel(node=5154, "Bacteroidetes")
p5 = collapse(p4, 5119) + geom_cladelabel(node=5119, "Firmicutes")

jpeg(filename = 'filename.jpeg', width = 1500, height = 4000, quality = 100)
p5
dev.off()

If I export p5 tree as a svg or jpeg, the node names I have added are not rotated with their branches - they are all oriented as normal text. The tip labels of the uncollapsed clades are rotated with the angle of the branches. How do I rotate the new node names? Or how do I apply a name to a collapsed clade such that it is treated as a new tip and new tip label, which would then rotate like the other tips (i.e., am I doing this wrong)?

2) Also, how do I rename internal nodes with a name of my choice, and then how do I export the tree file (not image, the tree as text in nexus or newick) with the node label changed? So for p2 clade in example above, how do I include the node name "Archaea" in an exported tree? I've been working with treeio and ape, and I can't find this option with either package.

Thanks in advance for any clarity on this!

best,
Laura

messages.subject_clean: geom_range not correctly displaying 95% HPDs for height from BEAST tree
messages.body_plain:
Hi Guangchuang,

Sorry, it was indeed little informative. I got some extra help yesterday and we were able to fix the issue for my tree.

I don't understand what causes the original problem, but no matter which field I use (height_range/0.95_HPD, length etc), geom_range never puts the bars in the correct place. We went around it by extracting the interval information from the tree and using using geom_segment. Code is:

a = read.beast("file.tre")

minmax = t(matrix(unlist(a@data$height_0.95_HPD),nrow=2))

bar_df = data.frame(node_id=as.integer(a@data$node),as.data.frame(minmax))
names(bar_df) = c('node_id','min','max')
bar_df = bar_df %>% filter(node_id > Ntip(a@phylo))

b = ggtree(a)
bar_df = bar_df %>% left_join(b$data, by=c('node_id'='node')) %>% select(node_id,min,max,y)

p <- revts(b) + geom_segment(aes(x=-min, y=y+1, xend=-max, yend=y+1), data=bar_df, color='blue') +
  geom_range(range='height_0.95_HPD', branch.length='height_median', color='red')
p

In the figure below, we have in blue the correct bars plotted with the geom_segment workaround. In red is the geom_range output of the height_0.95_HPD. You can see the wrong red bars are displaced to the right on the x axis, but not by a constant amount. Some nodes are basically fine, but some other are very different, e.g. the root.

Hope this helps some people. I would say be careful with the ranges, check they match your tree in FigTree our something.
I would be glad to learn if anybody else has fixed this is a different way using just geom_range.

Thanks!

p1 = ggtree(tr, layout = 'circular') + geom_tiplab2(color="black"

)

p3 = collapse(p2, 10, "Clade BC")

p3 + geom_nodelab(aes(subset = node == 10 | node == 11, angle=angle), hjust=-.1)

You need to install github version of ggplot2 and ggtree (v >= 1.13.0.005) to have this new feature of setting clade_name.
